changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/10106-settled-schema-equal-payload.md`

- names `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md` — edited by this change

  > The hook refetches `getObjectSchema` whenever the adapter identity changes, and every consumer its doc comment instructs — `ObjectGantt`, `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectView`, `ObjectTimeline`, `ObjectGallery` — keys its record fetch on the returned `def`, which is what `AGENTS.md` §5 commandment #10 tells a consumer to do (key on the payload, never on a memo identity). The producer half of that same sentence is what this fixes: a byte-identical answer arriving as a fresh object re-fired every one of those fetches, and the duplicate query carried the same `$expand` set as the one before it. Measured first-hand on `ObjectGantt` with an instrumented adapter, with a control swap in the same command; the counts, and the control that makes them a discrimination rather than a counting artefact, are asserted by `packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/useSettledSchema.equalPayload-10106.test.tsx` (objectui#10106).

### `.changeset/6357-basechema-bind-declaration.md`

- names `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md` — edited by this change

  > `bind` was read by ten production sites and declared by no schema shape. It resolved as `any` through `BaseSchema`'s index signature and rode `.passthrough()` on the validator, while three separate documents taught it as an authorable key of *every* node: this repo's own `AGENTS.md` §4 ("Every node in the UI tree follows this shape (`@object-ui/types`)"), the published agent-facing `skills/objectui/rules/protocol.md` ("Every UI component node MUST follow this shape"), and `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx`. So the agent-facing protocol told authors to write a key the published types did not know existed.

### `.changeset/6505-predicate-valued-gate-rules.md`

- names `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md` — edited by this change

  > **The accept set widens to what the protocol already declares and the runtime already accepts, not beyond it.** `AGENTS.md` §4 declares both keys as expressions, `SchemaRenderer` evaluates them through `hasDeclaredPredicate` + `evaluateCondition`, `@objectstack/spec` normalizes every authored predicate into a `{ dialect, source }` envelope, and the objectui#3862 / objectui#3955 rulings are entirely about which expression spellings count as declared. This table was the one place in the repo that disagreed, so this restores declared = enforced rather than changing a contract.

### `.changeset/7122-spec-17-3-0-parity-reconciliation.md`

- names `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md` — edited by this change

  > Two breaking consequences for a consumer that names the type directly. **(1)** It no longer declares `editMode`; the key is now carried by the spec's `ServiceObject`, so `ObjectSchemaMetadata` still has it, but code written against the extension type ALONE loses it. **(2)** `interface` → type alias also ends **declaration merging**: a consumer that reopened `declare module '@object-ui/types' { interface ObjectSchemaClientExtensions { … } }` to add its own client-side member no longer compiles, because an alias cannot be reopened. `minor` rather than `major` per `AGENTS.md`'s version-alignment rule — objectui's own breaking changes are graded `minor` with the semantics stated in the body, since any `major` in the fixed group would push all 39 packages off `@objectstack`'s major.

### `.changeset/7714-lookup-draft-stays-client-side.md`

- names `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS.md` — edited by this change

  > `minor` rather than `major` per `AGENTS.md`: objectui's major tracks `@objectstack`'s, so objectui's own breaking changes ship as `minor` with the breaking semantics stated.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `0cf2d6644` (merge-base with origin/main): 1 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1262 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1829 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35707170526)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `074b86db91d561802347966bd2efa07571bf5361`

### ① Derived judgments

Rendered in-seat by the skills seat 1 session at the served tier the maintainer named on this date (the fable tier word; ruling record objectstack#7623 comment 5771798588). The contract is the card's measured claim: the attribution-footer append is conditional on absence, not unconditional and not `PATCH`-only.

- **(a) One clause moves, nothing else — right.** `git diff origin/main 074b86d -- AGENTS.md` is +3 / −1: the third item of the six-item GitHub body-mutation list is rewritten (922 bytes) and gains two sub-bullets (521 and 864 bytes); items ①, ②, ④, ⑤, ⑥ and the two advice lines are byte-unchanged (measured by this seat: one line removed, three added, 589 → 591 lines). objectui has no `AGENTS.md` line ratchet or width cap; the file's own landing clause is a kilobyte, so the length is in style.
- **(b) The rewritten rule is the measured truth — right.** Sources, all first-hand: the card's four writes (+58 when absent on comment `POST`; 0 on comment `PATCH` with a footer already present), the addendum's six issue-body `PATCH` writes with pre-registered predictions (6 / 6, +58, verbatim concatenation), this seat's own PR-body `PATCH` writes this shift (10567 → 10625, 9225 → 9283, 15370 → 15428 — every one +58 with no footer sent, the one line in the new text the dev flagged as resting on the seat's reading, confirmed here), and the dev's two pre-registered readings in this run — `POST /pulls` with a session-URL footer: −1 (a stripped trailing newline), no append; the report comment `POST` with a bare footer: net 0, 53 separator positions rewritten, no append, one footer. The old sentence would have required two footers on the last two. The hazard the title names (a seat strips its own footer to dodge a duplicate and ships none) is now stated as the prohibition 「⛔ 永不剥自己的 footer」.
- **(c) The two sub-bullets do not overclaim — right.** The first names which half was measured on which channel and the one empty cell (issue / PR body `PATCH` sent a footer-terminated body) with 「⛔ 别把空格子读成已测」; the second states that a zero byte delta is not byte identity (the comment endpoint rewrites the separator: −1 trailing newline, +1 newline before `---`), prescribes read-back by first differing byte index, and declares the footer-recognition predicate unmeasured, flagging the second-hand session-URL report as 「二手读数,⛔ 别当判据用」. The dev's own `POST /pulls` reading (a session-URL footer recognised as present) is kept in the report and not written into the clause — the seat takes the dev's option A: a reading on one endpoint is not evidence for another, and writing a near-miss in is the over-generalisation being repaired.
- **(d) Cross-references — right.** No new cross-file `path:line` citation (`check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` reads 0 new; objectui bans them at `AGENTS.md:108`); the sibling objectui#9908 (the `POST` half) is answered by the same sentence and closes on its falsified premise at its take.
- **(e) Gates — re-run by this seat on its own worktree at this head:** `check-control-bytes` OK, `check-changeset-presence` (no changeset owed — 0 published source changed), `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` 0, `check-doc-links` valid, `check-shell-escape-residue` OK; `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test AGENTS.md` exit 3 — GOVERNED, the Tier H basis, not a red. objectui has no `dispatch-gates.mjs`; the gate family was derived by hand from `package.json` and the workflows, and `lint.yml` skips a markdown-only diff by its own paths-ignore — stated, not assumed.

### ② Semver level

None — a governed instruction file; no package source, no changeset owed (`check-changeset-presence` measured 0 published files), no label written (objectui path labels are `labeler.yml`'s; `documentation` was applied by it).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`pnpm install` not run in the worktree** — declared narrowing; every applicable gate is a dependency-free node script and produced a real verdict. Accepted.
- **The dev sent both budgeted writes WITH a footer attached and predicted no append**, instead of the seat's suggested 「sent + 58」 reading: the conditionality half is the one under test and the one where the card's row 2 and objectui#9908 disagree; both outcomes were safe for the artefact. A better measurement than the one asked for — accepted, and the predictions were registered in the PR body before the requests.
- **Length**: three lines of 922 / 521 / 864 bytes — long, in a file whose landing clause is longer; no cap exists here. Accepted; the 维护者速读 tells the maintainer where to read.
- **CI at this head**: objectui's test shards were `in_progress` at the seat's read (a markdown-only diff — `ci.yml`'s own switch skips the expensive steps); Tier H — the maintainer merges; the seat reports the checks green before that hand-off.
- **Two open questions from the dev**, both decided here: (1) the `POST /pulls` reading stays in the report, ⛔ not in the clause (option A); (2) the empty matrix cell is filled only opportunistically from a body `PATCH` a seat already owes, with the prediction registered first — ⛔ never as a synthetic probe.
